author: Jin_Int
title: “Because for me, the meaning of life is embodied in the possibility for women to live freely.”
content:
Dear comrades… Bearers of the consciousness and work of Jineolojî, builders of a free life.

Ever since childhood, I have carried within me a quest: to witness the liberation of women and to open up a space for them to live a life worthy of them. This quest became even more profound when my playmate could no longer play with me, and my sister was sent away in exchange for a sack of bulgur. In the silent resistance of the village women and resurgence of what remained of the goddesses, I saw that liberation was possible. I, too, followed that faith. I have always followed in their footsteps. For I knew that society’s deepest wound was the enslavement of women. Without this understanding, freedom, equality and true democracy would have been impossible.

In proposing Jineolojî, my aim was not merely to create a concept. Our most vital task to bequeath to history would be to redefine women’s existence within its historical and social reality and to free women from the role of object, making them subjects. I wanted to bring to light the wisdom of the goddess – hidden by thousands of years of patriarchal civilisation – and the woman-centred way of life of the Neolithic era. The dagger lodged in the back of society was the enslavement of women; without removing that dagger, no social problem could be resolved at its root.
